summary: Ravi M. Gupta is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Boise State University and the University of Oxford. His academic career includes teaching at Florida, Centre College, William & Mary, and holding a chair at Utah State.

Ravindra Singh Bisht is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned degrees from the University of Lucknow, the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and Kumaun University, and held key posts in Punjab, Haryana, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

Raymond Allchin (1923–2010) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate under K. de B. Codrington at the University of London and held academic posts at SOAS, the University of Cambridge, and the Ancient India & Iran Trust.

Raymond West (1832–1912) was an Indologist who studied under Martin Haug. He served as a judge of the Bombay High Court, Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and Reader in Indian Law at the University of Cambridge.
Reb Anderson is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Richard Baker. He served as abbot of the San Francisco Zen Center from around 1986 to 1995.
Reb Gongwa Jamyang Chökyi Lodrö studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok and Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro.

Rebecca Redwood French works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Mentored by Leopold Pospisil, Stanley Weinstein, and others, she earned degrees from the University of Washington and Yale, holding law faculty posts at the University of Colorado and University at Buffalo.

Reginald A. Ray works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Mircea Eliade, Joseph M. Kitagawa, and Chögyam Trungpa, and held teaching posts at the University of Colorado and Naropa University.

Reginald Horace Blyth (1898–1964) was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at the University of London. He held academic posts at Keijo Imperial University and Kanazawa University.
Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from roughly 1949 to 1953 and later served as a professor there from around 1974 to 2000.
Reiho Masunaga (1902–1981) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Kaiten Nukariya and taught at Komazawa University from around 1930 to 1973.

Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, she held positions at the University of Texas at Austin, the University of Alabama, and Dartmouth College.

Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Kyoto Women's University, and Ryukoku University.

Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Nancy and Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as a professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and the University of Heidelberg from 1977.
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin in the 1980s and at Göttingen State and University Library in 2008.

Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a linguist who completed his habilitation at the University of Leipzig. He spent his career at Leipzig, serving as assistant professor from 1832 and as professor from 1849 to 1870.

Reinhold Niebuhr (1892–1971) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School, and served on the faculty at Union Theological Seminary from around 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Jena. He taught at St Augustine's College and served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and librarian for the India Office.
Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich, where she studied under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner.
Renjū Akamatsu (1841–1919) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.
